html:
Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on 20 September 2017 as a strong category 4 storm, two weeks after Irma. It was the worst natural disaster in the island's modern history.

It destroyed the power grid, leaving the whole island without electricity, some areas for most of a year. Water, roads and phones failed. A study for the island's government later estimated that about 3,000 people died as a result, many from lack of power and care.

The slow federal response angered Puerto Ricans and raised the question of their unequal status. Coming on top of the debt crisis, it drove many to the mainland. Maria had devastated Dominica two days before.
sum: Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico on 20 September 2017 as a strong category 4 storm, two weeks after Irma. It was the worst natural disaster in the island's modern history.
